newsitem.title: GERMANY: Spectacular operation saves east German dike.
newsitem.headline: Spectacular operation saves east German dike.

text.p: A spectacular overnight operation involving hundreds of soldiers and several helicopters prevented the complete collapse of a dike in flood-hit eastern Germany, officials said on Tuesday.

A team of 700 soldiers and relief workers battled through the night to shore up a section of the dike on the Oder River near the village of Hohenwutzen, which had collapsed and nearly caused a total break in the dam.

"A six to seven metre section of the dike in the area that is especially endangered collapsed overnight," said a spokesman for Brandenburg state. "There is a danger at this location that the dike foundations could become unstable."

Officials said up to nine helicopters had flown continuously throughout the night as workers filled 200,000 sandbags to plug the gap in the dike. The situation throughout the region remained critical, officials said.
Chancellor Helmut Kohl was scheduled to interrupt his summer holiday later on Tuesday to visit soldiers, relief workers and residents along the Oder.

In an area south of the scene of the overnight drama, where the Oder and Neisse rivers meet, relief aid workers had begun building an 800-metre secondary dike, anticipating a possible break in the main dam near the town of Ratzdorf.
Brandenburg officials said a new wave of high water was approaching Ratzdorf and would reach the most critical areas of the east German stretch of the Oder by afternoon.
The floods have claimed more than a hundred lives in neighbouring Poland and the Czech Republic.

Germany has so far escaped the worst of the damage but thousands of residents have already been evacuated from their homes and thousands more are on standby to leave at a moment's notice if the dikes give way.
